In [[category theory]], a branch of mathematics, an '''adequate subcategory''' of a [[category (mathematics)|category]] ''X'' is an analog of a [[dense subspace]] in topology for [[presheaf (category theory)|presheaves]]: namely, a subcategory <math>i : A \hookrightarrow X</math> such that the restriction of the [[Yoneda embedding]] <math>X \hookrightarrow \mathbf{P}(X)</math> along <math>i</math> is still [[fully faithful]].<ref>§ 2 in {{cite journal |last1=Lawvere |first1=F. W. |author-link1=F. W. Lawvere |title=Metric spaces, generalized logic and closed categories |journal=Reprints in Theory and Applications of Categories |date=2002 |issue=1 |pages=1–37 |url=http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/reprints/articles/1/tr1.pdf}}</ref> The notion was introduced by [[John Isbell|Isbell]] in 1960. Note some authors<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lurie |first=Jacob |author-link=Jacob Lurie |title=Kerodon |url=https://kerodon.net/tag/03V8 |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=kerodon.net |language=en}}</ref> use the term '''dense subcategory''' for this notion, although it can mean a different thing in other contexts.
